info.title: Onyx Ledger API
info.description: AI-powered Canadian tax optimization SaaS — educational, not filing.

post.description:
Create an account.

Throttled on the same class as login. Registration is not a credential test,
but it is unauthenticated, it writes two rows and computes an Argon2 hash,
and — because it must say whether an address is already taken — an
unthrottled version is a fast account-enumeration oracle. The throttle does
not remove that disclosure; it bounds how quickly it can be harvested.

schema.title: Response Register Api V1 Auth Register Post

post.description:
Exchange credentials for a token pair.

Admission runs FIRST — before the user lookup and before Argon2 — so a
refused attempt costs one indexed UPSERT instead of a deliberately expensive
key derivation. See `app.services.admission.auth`.

Rotate a refresh token.

Also a credential surface: a stolen or guessed refresh token is presented
here. The identity scope is keyed on the presented TOKEN rather than on an
email, because that is the only identity claim the request carries — it
bounds how fast one token can be hammered, while the address scope bounds
hammering with a rotating supply of them.

schema.title: Response Get Me Api V1 Users Me Get

post.description:
Record an income source.

NORMAL_WRITE: cheap per call, and an UNBOUNDED row creator. RLS keeps the
rows inside one tenant, which bounds who can read them and not how many
there are — a script here fills a tenant's own financial tables and, through
them, the cost of every later analysis over that year.

schema.title: Response List Income Api V1 Financials Income Get

post.description:
Record an actual RRSP/FHSA contribution for a tax year — a fact the
baseline analysis reads, as opposed to a scenario lever, which models a
contribution not yet made.

schema.title: Response List Registered Accounts Api V1 Financials Registered Accounts Get
Response Add Expense Api V1 Financials Expenses Post

delete.description:
Delete one owned income source.

The tax year is a required query parameter rather than something the server
looks up, because the table is partitioned on it and the primary key is
(id, tax_year). Supplying it prunes to one partition; without it the server
would have to scan every year to find a row the caller already knows the
year of.

It is NOT authorization — ownership is checked against the row, and a wrong
year simply finds nothing.

NORMAL_WRITE admission: cheap per call, but it is a mutation and an
unbounded caller should not be able to drive deletions in a loop for free.

schema.title: Response Delete Income Api V1 Financials Income  Income Id  Delete

delete.description: Delete one owned expense. Same contract as `delete_income`.

schema.title: Response Delete Expense Api V1 Financials Expenses  Expense Id  Delete

get.description: Published tax rules in force for a year (the versioned KB, read-only).

schema.title: Response List Published Rules Api V1 Tax Rules Get
Response List Analyses Api V1 Analysis Get

post.description:
Run a full analysis. Admission-controlled: this is a synchronous engine
run plus a rules evaluation plus a frozen snapshot, and a double-click has
nothing to add while the first one is still going.

schema.title: Response List Recommendations Api V1 Recommendations Get
Response List Documents Api V1 Documents Get

post.description:
Register a document and hand back a presigned upload URL.

TWO size checks, and only the second one is a bound.

The bytes never pass through this process — they go straight to object
storage — so the check here is on the DECLARED size. It is an early, cheap
refusal that catches an honest client and saves a round trip. It is NOT
enforcement: a caller that wants to store 30 MB under a 25 MB limit simply
declares 1 MB.

Enforcement is the ceiling attached to the presigned authorization itself,
which the store applies to the bytes that actually arrive
(`ObjectStorage.presign_put(..., max_bytes=...)`; in S3 that is a POST
policy `content-length-range` condition). The declaration is honoured too,
where it is tighter — a client that says 1 MB and sends 5 MB is refused
even though 5 MB is under the platform limit.

schema.title: Response Create Upload Api V1 Documents Post

post.description:
Extract fields from an uploaded document.

Uploading and PROCESSING are separate costs, and this is the expensive one:
it is the classic path for turning one cheap request into minutes of CPU.
Bounded concurrency, and a dedupe key on the document so re-processing the
same immutable document cannot create unlimited work.

schema.title: Response Process Api V1 Documents  Document Id  Process Post

post.description:
Turn a confirmed extraction into income/expense rows.

NORMAL_WRITE rather than DOCUMENT_PROCESS: no extraction runs here, but each
call writes a row per extracted field plus a provenance link, so repeated
confirmation of one document is an unbounded row creator.

schema.title: Response Confirm Api V1 Documents  Document Id  Confirm Post

delete.description:
Delete one owned document: binary, extraction and all.

The document is named by ID and the object key is resolved SERVER-SIDE from
the owned row. A client never supplies a bucket or a key — a caller able to
name its own key could ask the platform to delete an arbitrary object,
including another tenant's, and the ownership check would never see it.

Synchronous, and deliberately so. The work is one object deletion and two
bounded statements, all of which comfortably fit inside a request; a 202
with a background job would add a durable queue, a worker and a state
machine to defer something that already finished. If object deletion ever
becomes slow enough to matter — a versioned bucket needing per-version
deletes — this returns 202 and grows the job then, on evidence.

NORMAL_WRITE admission: cheap per call, but it is a mutation and an
unbounded caller should not be able to drive object-store deletions in a
loop for free.

schema.title: Response Delete Document Api V1 Documents  Document Id  Delete

get.description:
The caller's own deletion status.

Lifecycle-exempt for the obvious reason: a user who has asked to be deleted
must still be able to see what happened to the request.

schema.title: Response Get Account Deletion Status Api V1 Account Deletion Get

post.description:
Request deletion of the CALLER'S OWN account.

The account is resolved from the authenticated token and nowhere else.
There is no path parameter and no body: an endpoint that accepted an account
id would be one authorization mistake away from letting anyone delete
anyone, and no amount of checking afterwards is as good as not offering the
parameter.

202 rather than 200: the request is durable and access is already gone, but
the purge it schedules has not run. Later 11B phases perform that, and until
they exist this deliberately cannot report completion.

Idempotent — a second request returns the same lifecycle rather than
starting another.

schema.title: Response Request Account Deletion Api V1 Account Deletion Post

post.description:
Open an empty conversation.

One INSERT, so it is a NORMAL_WRITE rather than an AI_EXPLAIN — but it is
still an unbounded row creator, and a loop against it costs the platform
storage without ever touching the expensive path.

schema.title: Response Create Conversation Api V1 Ai Conversations Post

post.description:
Ask within an existing conversation.

AI_EXPLAIN, because the work is retrieval plus a completion: a vector search
over the year's published rules, a lazy REINDEX of that year on first use,
and a provider call whose cost lives outside this process. That last part is
exactly why the ceiling has to be here — nothing downstream of this handler
is in a position to refuse.

schema.title: Response Ask Api V1 Ai Conversations  Conversation Id  Messages Post
Response List Messages Api V1 Ai Conversations  Conversation Id  Messages Get

post.description: One-shot: starts a new conversation and answers.

schema.title: Response Ask New Api V1 Ai Ask Post

post.summary: Generate a validated explanation of a governed result
post.description: Renders the caller's own sealed/governed result as a customer-safe explanation. The renderer holds no authority: every number, verdict, citation, deadline and assumption comes from the assembled governed input, and generated output survives only if the deterministic validators accept it — otherwise the deterministic template renderer answers. No internal hashes are exposed.

Operator login.

Throttled on the same class as user login, and if anything it matters more
here: the population of valid operator addresses is tiny, which makes this
the highest-value guessing target in the product.

schema.title: Response Admin Login Api V1 Admin Auth Login Post

post.description:
Raw dataset -> Extract -> Validate -> Transform -> DRAFT rule versions +
a pending four-eyes change request per rule.

The same cost class as a TKMS import: it parses a whole dataset and writes a
draft version plus a change request per rule. Bounded on bytes first, then
on the acting operator's import allowance.

schema.title: Response Create Ingestion Job Api V1 Admin Ingestion Jobs Post
Response Approve Change Request Api V1 Admin Change Requests  Change Request Id  Approve Post

post.description:
Activate an approved rule version.

Guarded on the ACTING OPERATOR, and the guard is outside the service call so
a refusal happens BEFORE activation — no version transitions to published,
and no freshness event is emitted for a publication that did not occur. A
guard placed inside the service, after the status change, would bound
nothing that matters: the invalidation storm is the cost, and it would
already have been paid.

schema.title: Response Publish Rule Api V1 Admin Rules  Version Id  Publish Post
Response List Rule Versions Api V1 Admin Rules Get
Response List Change Requests Api V1 Admin Change Requests Get

post.description:
Ingest a legislation document and run the governed pipeline.

THREE bounds, in the order they cost something:

  1. the payload's real encoded size, refused before a row is written;
  2. admission on the acting operator, refused before parsing starts;
  3. `MAX_IMPORT_ROWS` inside `ImportService.extract`, which is where the
     staged-row count is actually known — a small document can expand into
     an enormous ruleset, so a byte bound does not imply a row bound.

Authorization comes FIRST, before the byte check and before admission: an
operator without `tkms.import` must not be able to spend an admission
allowance, and must not learn anything from the difference between "too
large" and "not permitted".

schema.title: Response Create Import Api V1 Tkms Imports Post
Response List Imports Api V1 Tkms Imports Get

post.description:
Re-run the pipeline for an existing job.

The same class as a fresh import, because it costs the same: it discards the
prior parse and re-executes every stage. Deduped on the job, so a retry
storm against one job resolves to the run already in flight rather than
stacking full re-parses of the same document.

schema.title: Response Reparse Import Api V1 Tkms Imports  Job Id  Reparse Post
Response Get Import Api V1 Tkms Imports  Job Id  Get
Response Get Extracted Api V1 Tkms Imports  Job Id  Extracted Get
Response Get Validation Api V1 Tkms Imports  Job Id  Validation Get
Response Get Compare Api V1 Tkms Versions  Version Id  Compare Get
Response Submit Version Api V1 Tkms Versions  Version Id  Submit Post
Response Approve Version Api V1 Tkms Versions  Version Id  Approve Post
Response Reject Version Api V1 Tkms Versions  Version Id  Reject Post

post.description:
Publish an approved version and reindex the knowledge base.

Costlier than the `/admin/rules/{id}/publish` path — it reindexes — and
guarded on the same class and the same principal. Refused BEFORE the
publication, so a rejected call leaves no published version, no reindex and
no freshness event behind.

Response Request Rollback Api V1 Tkms Rules  Rule Id  Rollback Post
Response Approve Rollback Api V1 Tkms Rollbacks  Rollback Id  Approve Post

post.summary: Run optimization over a completed analysis
post.description: Invokes the certified optimization orchestrator for the caller's own analysis. Admission control, idempotent spec-hash resolution, sealing and replay identity all live in the orchestrator — this route adds authentication and the typed constraint contract, nothing else.
Accepts typed lever codes and structured assumptions ONLY. There is no field through which an engine input can be named or a computation supplied.

parameters.name: include_archived

schema.description: Archived scenarios are hidden, not deleted.
schema.title: Include Archived

parameters.description: Archived scenarios are hidden, not deleted.

schema.title: Response List Scenarios Api V1 Ioe Scenarios Get

get.summary: Read a scenario, re-evaluating its freshness
get.description: Freshness is evaluated on this read and any transition is persisted, so a stale result is never returned labelled current. The stored result itself is never modified.

delete.description: This is an ARCHIVE, not a deletion. The result, the applied-change trace, the pinned specification and the audit events all survive.

post.summary: Re-run a scenario against today's world
post.description: Creates a NEW scenario and marks the original superseded. The historical result keeps its own pinned versions and its own numbers.

get.description: Refuses the comparison unless both scenarios are owned by the caller, completed, sealed, and compatible on baseline, tax year, jurisdiction, objective policy and result schema. Deltas are kept separate by concept.

get.summary: What would change if you did this
get.description: The Before-You-Act comparison: the difference between this scenario's frozen baseline and its sealed counterfactual. Read entirely from sealed rows — no tax is computed, no rule is evaluated, no current document is read. A scenario whose seal cannot answer for a comparison family is refused rather than partially compared. Reports what changed; it does not recommend a course of action.

parameters.name: include_unchanged

schema.description: Render records that did not change. Presentation only: the summary counts and the comparison hash are identical either way.
schema.title: Include Unchanged

parameters.description: Render records that did not change. Presentation only: the summary counts and the comparison hash are identical either way.

get.summary: The Tax Assurance Map for one tax year
get.description: The current standing of the caller's tax position, derived deterministically from governed state: opportunities, evidence readiness, deadlines, assumptions, and a documented review-next order. Reports standing only — it computes no tax, decides no eligibility, and makes no recommendation beyond its documented presentation order. A family with no governing run reads UNAVAILABLE, never as an empty READY.

parameters.name: as_of

schema.description: Evaluation date for deadline urgency, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC). The only field the clock touches.
schema.title: As Of

parameters.description: Evaluation date for deadline urgency, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC). The only field the clock touches.

schema.title: Response List Decision Journals Api V1 Ioe Decision Journal Get

post.summary: Open a decision thread from a sealed scenario
post.description: Records that the user is CONSIDERING a decision about a scenario they own, pinning the sealed artifact identities that informed it. Append-only from here: every later change is a new event. Retrying with the same request_id returns the thread already created.

get.summary: Read one decision thread with its full history
get.description: The append-only history, the projection derived from it, the pinned scenario reference, and governed evidence context — sealed readiness as recorded, current observed readiness as it stands now. A user report of an action is presented as a report, never as verification.

post.description: Appends the user's declaration — PROCEED, DEFER, DECLINE, or back to CONSIDERING. A change of mind appends; nothing is rewritten. PROCEED records intent and is never treated as proof an action occurred.

post.summary: Report that the action was taken
post.description: Records the user's report that they acted, optionally with the date they say it happened. A self-report: the response continues to label execution USER_REPORTED, and evidence context remains a separate, governed observation.

get.summary: Read the sealed strategy portfolio for an optimization run
get.description: Every figure is read from the sealed portfolio row. The total is not rebuilt from members, and no recommendation amounts are summed.

get.summary: Read multi-year projections for a run
get.description: Projections are returned SEPARATELY and are never part of any current-year total. Always an object with a status: a run with no rule-authorized projection returns an explicit not_generated status rather than a misleading null.

Whether the SEALED result can still be reproduced from its own pinned inputs. A different question from freshness: a result can be stale and reproducible, or current and non-reproducible. Reads stored metadata only — this never triggers a replay. Hashes are not exposed.

post.description: Re-executes the sealed calculation against its pinned dependencies and records the outcome. The historical result is never modified, regenerated, or repaired — a mismatch is recorded and preserved, not corrected. Returns 409 while another verification of the same entity is already running.

get.summary: The current lifecycle of every governed opportunity
get.description: Joins the Tax Assurance Map with the Decision Journal: availability, the user's decision, whether they reported acting, evidence readiness, the governed deadline and its timing band, freshness and integrity — seven axes that never collapse into one another. Expired opportunities stay visible with timing EXPIRED rather than disappearing. Reports state; it computes no tax, evaluates no rule, and ranks nothing the optimizer has not already ranked.

parameters.name: as_of

schema.description: Evaluation date for deadline timing, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC). The only field the clock touches.
schema.title: As Of

parameters.description: Evaluation date for deadline timing, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC). The only field the clock touches.

get.summary: What materially changed since the last acknowledged state
get.description: Compares current governed state against the state the user last explicitly acknowledged. SIDE-EFFECT FREE: reading never advances the baseline, so refreshing shows the same unacknowledged changes until they are acknowledged. Reports band transitions, not countdowns — a deadline moving from 38 to 37 days is not a change; NORMAL becoming APPROACHING is. On first use `baseline_status` is NO_BASELINE and the change list is empty rather than restating current state as arrivals.

parameters.name: as_of

schema.description: Evaluation date for the timing bands, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC).
schema.title: As Of

parameters.description: Evaluation date for the timing bands, echoed in the response. Defaults to today (UTC).

post.summary: Acknowledge the reviewed state, establishing a new baseline
post.description: The ONLY operation that advances the retention baseline. The client echoes the `current_snapshot_hash` it reviewed and the baseline it compared against; if either has moved the request is refused with 409 rather than silently recording that the user reviewed changes they never saw. Retrying with the same `request_id` returns the checkpoint the first attempt created.

snapshot_hash.title: Snapshot Hash
snapshot_hash.description: The `current_snapshot_hash` from the changes response being acknowledged. Refused with 409 if current state has moved since.

baseline_checkpoint_id.title: Baseline Checkpoint Id
baseline_checkpoint_id.description: The `baseline_checkpoint.id` the client compared against, or null when establishing the first baseline. Refused with 409 if another acknowledgement superseded it first.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Idempotency key. A retry returns the same checkpoint.

AcknowledgeChangesRequest.title: AcknowledgeChangesRequest
AcknowledgeChangesRequest.description:
Acknowledge the exact state the client reviewed.

Both tokens are required rather than convenient. `snapshot_hash` says WHICH
STATE was reviewed; `baseline_checkpoint_id` says WHICH BASELINE it was
reviewed against. Together they make a stale acknowledgement impossible to
express by accident, which matters because the failure mode is silent:
recording that a user reviewed changes they never saw.

AppliedChangeOut.title: AppliedChangeOut
AppliedChangeOut.description:
One field the levers moved. Records the FIELD the registry wrote, never
the user's other financial inputs.

AssumptionInput-Input.title: AssumptionInput
AssumptionInput-Input.description:
A registered assumption code plus exactly one typed value.

Origin fields are CLOSED vocabularies. The full sets are expressible here
because this model also renders platform-attached assumptions on output
surfaces — but on input the domain parser further requires
`source="user"` / `certainty="user_asserted"`: an API payload states the
caller's own declaration and cannot claim platform or statutory
provenance.

AssumptionInput-Output.title: AssumptionInput
AssumptionInput-Output.description:
A registered assumption code plus exactly one typed value.

Origin fields are CLOSED vocabularies. The full sets are expressible here
because this model also renders platform-attached assumptions on output
surfaces — but on input the domain parser further requires
`source="user"` / `certainty="user_asserted"`: an API payload states the
caller's own declaration and cannot claim platform or statutory
provenance.

AssumptionNoteV1.title: AssumptionNoteV1
AssumptionNoteV1.description: One assumption, rendered with its TRUE origin preserved.

AssuranceSummaryOut.title: AssuranceSummaryOut
AssuranceSummaryOut.description:
Multi-dimensional counts. Deliberately not a single score — no governed
model defines what such a number would measure.

AttentionFlagsOut.title: AttentionFlagsOut
AttentionFlagsOut.description:
Structured flags instead of a score — each one a governed fact a client
can render, explain, or ignore independently.

BaselineCheckpointOut.title: BaselineCheckpointOut
BaselineCheckpointOut.description: Which acknowledged state the comparison was measured from.

BeforeYouActComparisonOut.title: BeforeYouActComparisonOut
BeforeYouActComparisonOut.description:
The whole product contract.

Change records are grouped by family rather than returned as one list, so a
client renders "what happens to your tax position" separately from "what you
would need to prove". A single flat list would push that classification onto
every client, and they would each do it differently.

ChangeOut.title: ChangeOut
ChangeOut.description:
One node that was added, removed, changed, or left alone.

`key` is the certified semantic identity. It is exposed because a client
needs a stable handle to correlate a record across two requests; it is not
an internal row id and resolves to nothing on its own.

ChangeSummaryOut.title: ChangeSummaryOut
ChangeSummaryOut.description: Transparent counts only — no composite score, and no money.

ComparisonSummaryOut.title: ComparisonSummaryOut
ComparisonSummaryOut.description:
Counts over the FULL comparison, before any presentation filtering.

They do not move when `include_unchanged` changes, because the summary
describes the comparison and the lists describe what was rendered.

subject_opportunity_code.title: Subject Opportunity Code
subject_opportunity_code.description: Optional governed opportunity code this decision is about.

CreateDecisionJournalRequest.title: CreateDecisionJournalRequest
CreateDecisionJournalRequest.description:
Open a decision thread from a scenario the caller owns.

`request_id` is the idempotency identity: a retried POST with the same id
returns the thread the first attempt created.

DeadlineOut.title: DeadlineOut
DeadlineOut.description:
A governed deadline. `days_remaining` and `urgency` are evaluated
against the response's `as_of` date, which is echoed at the top level so
the derivation is reproducible.

DecisionJournalDetailOut.title: DecisionJournalDetailOut
DecisionJournalDetailOut.description:
The full thread: everything the summary carries, plus the history that
produced it and the governed evidence context.

DecisionJournalSummaryOut.title: DecisionJournalSummaryOut
DecisionJournalSummaryOut.description: One thread as the list renders it: identity, linkage, projection.

EvidenceContextOut.title: EvidenceContextOut
EvidenceContextOut.description:
Governed evidence semantics beside the journal.

`sealed_readiness` is what the sealed scenario recorded and will never
change. `current_observed_readiness` is the same certified primitive over
the documents held NOW — labeled current because it moves. Neither is
verification that the reported action occurred.

EvidenceReadinessRowOut.title: EvidenceReadinessRowOut
EvidenceReadinessRowOut.description:
One governed requirement resolved to a readiness verdict. Identity is
the document TYPE — never a document id, bucket, key, or hash.

EvidenceRequirementOut.title: EvidenceRequirementOut
EvidenceRequirementOut.description:
One governed document requirement. Identity is the document TYPE —
never a document id, bucket, object key or content hash.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Educational information only. This is not tax advice, not a filing, and is not submitted to the CRA.

ExplanationEnvelopeOut.title: ExplanationEnvelopeOut
ExplanationEnvelopeOut.description:
The API response: the validated explanation plus non-sensitive
metadata. No internal hashes, no subject binding.

ExplanationOutputV1.title: ExplanationOutputV1
ExplanationOutputV1.description:
Everything the renderer may say.

Absence is meaningful: an optional field left null says "not applicable to
this explanation", never "fill it with something plausible". `citation_refs`
must be a subset of the input's citation ids and `value_refs_used` of its
value-table keys — both enforced mechanically by the validators, not by
convention.

subject_id.title: Subject Id
subject_id.description: The authoritative subject: analysis id (TAX_POSITION), opportunity source id or code (OPPORTUNITY), optimization run id (PORTFOLIO), scenario id (SCENARIO, COMPARISON), decision-journal id (EVIDENCE_READINESS). Unused for WHAT_CHANGED.

ExplanationRequest.title: ExplanationRequest
ExplanationRequest.description:
What to explain. No tax facts can be supplied here — the assembler
loads the authenticated user's authoritative subject through the owning
tenant-isolated services, and the renderer sees only what they return.

FamilyApplicabilityOut.title: FamilyApplicabilityOut
FamilyApplicabilityOut.description:
Why a family is comparable, or why it is not.

Carried so a reader can tell a family that is comparable and empty from one
that does not apply at all. Dropping this would leave "no resources shown"
and "resources are not a single-scenario concept" looking identical, which
is the distinction the whole comparison rests on.

FamilyAssuranceOut.title: FamilyAssuranceOut
FamilyAssuranceOut.description:
One family's standing. UNAVAILABLE with zero items and READY with zero
items are different claims, and this row is what keeps them different.

FieldChangeOut.title: FieldChangeOut
FieldChangeOut.description:
One field that moved, with the arithmetic only where it is defined.

`delta` is present only for a governed numeric field whose two sides share a
declared unit. Its absence is meaningful: it says the domain does not define
a difference here, not that the difference is zero.

FieldTransitionOut.title: FieldTransitionOut
FieldTransitionOut.description: One field's before and after. Structured, never a rendered diff.

FreshnessOut.title: FreshnessOut
FreshnessOut.description: Whether the result is still a statement about today's world.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Replay verification checks that a stored result can be reproduced from its own sealed inputs. It is not a statement of tax correctness.

IntegrityCheckOut.title: IntegrityCheckOut
IntegrityCheckOut.description: The outcome of one explicit verification request.

integrity_state.title: Integrity State
integrity_state.description: User-visible classification: not_checked | verified | non_reproducible | unavailable | legacy_unverifiable. A mismatch is reported as non_reproducible; an unavailable explained by the result's age is reported as legacy_unverifiable.

integrity_warning.title: Integrity Warning
integrity_warning.description: Plain statement about REPRODUCIBILITY only. It says nothing about whether the figure is correct, accepted by the CRA, or legally sound.

execution_policy.title: Execution Policy
execution_policy.description: How this result's inputs were obtained. `frozen_snapshot_v1` means it was calculated exclusively from the pinned analysis snapshot. A `*_legacy` value means it predates that guarantee and may not reproduce; legacy rows are never relabelled. Null on an entity that records no policy of its own — a portfolio's is its run's.

IntegrityOut.title: IntegrityOut
IntegrityOut.description:
Whether the SEALED result can still be reproduced.

A different question from freshness, and never merged with it: a result can
be stale and perfectly reproducible, or current and non-reproducible. The
second is far more serious and must not hide behind the word "stale".

`integrity_state` is what a client should render, and it distinguishes four
cases the two-word status cannot:

  verified             reproduced from its own pinned inputs
  non_reproducible     a `mismatch` — the replay ran on a result that was
                       contractually reproducible and produced a DIFFERENT
                       identity. The only case that implies a defect.
  unavailable          a pinned artifact is missing, replaced, malformed or
                       fails its identity check. NOTHING was compared, and
                       the next sweep may well verify it.
  legacy_unverifiable  the result predates the frozen-input guarantee, so it
                       never carried what a replay would need. Not a defect
                       and not fixable by waiting — re-run it.

`integrity_reason_code` is the machine-readable axis; `integrity_state` is
the human one. A client that counts failures should count
`non_reproducible`, never `legacy_unverifiable`.

Hashes are deliberately absent. They are restricted diagnostic metadata,
they are not proof of ownership, and an ordinary user has no use for them.

JournalLinkOut.title: JournalLinkOut
JournalLinkOut.description:
Which Journal thread the reported decision came from.

`thread_count` is exposed rather than hidden: a user who decided twice has
two threads, and showing only the latest without saying so would make the
others look as if they never happened. The Journal remains the history
authority for all of them.

lever_code.title: Lever Code
lever_code.description: A registered lever code. Never an engine field name.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Values for the parameters the registry declares for this lever. Undeclared parameters are rejected.

LeverInput-Input.title: LeverInput
LeverInput-Input.description:
A lever named by CODE with declared parameters.

`model_config` forbids extra fields, so a request carrying `field`, `patch`,
`formula`, or any other mutation shape is rejected by the schema before it
reaches the domain parser — and, just as importantly, such a field never
appears in the OpenAPI document as something a caller might supply.

lever_code.title: Lever Code
lever_code.description: A registered lever code. Never an engine field name.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Values for the parameters the registry declares for this lever. Undeclared parameters are rejected.

LeverInput-Output.title: LeverInput
LeverInput-Output.description:
A lever named by CODE with declared parameters.

`model_config` forbids extra fields, so a request carrying `field`, `patch`,
`formula`, or any other mutation shape is rejected by the schema before it
reaches the domain parser — and, just as importantly, such a field never
appears in the OpenAPI document as something a caller might supply.

LifecycleDeadlineOut.title: LifecycleDeadlineOut
LifecycleDeadlineOut.description:
The governed deadline, verbatim. Never fabricated — its absence is
reported as `deadline: null` with `timing: NO_DEADLINE`.

change_id.title: Change Id
change_id.description: Deterministic identity, bound to both snapshot hashes and the transition. Stable across repeated reads of the same two states, so a future delivery path can deduplicate on it. Never a row id.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: The governed opportunity code, or the Assurance family.

MaterialChangeOut.title: MaterialChangeOut
MaterialChangeOut.description: One semantic event about one governed subject.

effect_type.title: Effect Type
effect_type.description: What KIND of money this is (current_year_tax_reduction, tax_deferral, refundable_benefit, liquidity_commitment, ...). Amounts of different effect types are never summed.

horizon_years.title: Horizon Years
horizon_years.description: 1 = current year only. A multi-year figure is never comparable with a current-year one.

is_permanent.title: Is Permanent
is_permanent.description: False for timing benefits such as a deferral.

MonetaryAmount.title: MonetaryAmount
MonetaryAmount.description:
A dollar figure that cannot be shown without its meaning.

`effect_type` is the field that stops different kinds of money being read as
interchangeable: a tax deferral is a timing benefit, a refundable benefit is
cash, and a liquidity commitment is money that must be available but is not
lost. They are never summed into one another.

horizon_year.title: Horizon Year
horizon_year.description: The final year of the horizon.

horizon_years.title: Horizon Years
horizon_years.description: Length of the horizon in years.

separation_note.title: Separation Note
separation_note.default: Projected figures are estimates over a multi-year horizon and are NOT included in any current-year total.

MultiYearProjectionOut.title: MultiYearProjectionOut
MultiYearProjectionOut.description:
Deliberately NOT part of any current-year total.

A multi-year projection rests on assumptions that a current-year engine
result does not. Merging the two would let assumption-laden figures inherit
the credibility of a deterministic calculation.

NextStepV1.title: NextStepV1
NextStepV1.description:
A next step that MUST reference a supplied structured action.

`action_ref` is a rules-authored `action_code`, or `resolution:<option>`
for a supplied portfolio-exclusion resolution option. Free-text steps
cannot become structured next steps.

standalone_potential.title: Standalone Potential
standalone_potential.description: Governed impact figure, sealed by the optimizer. Not recomputed here.

OpportunityAssuranceOut.title: OpportunityAssuranceOut
OpportunityAssuranceOut.description:
One opportunity's standing. Every figure was produced by the governed
authority that owns it; nothing in this payload was computed at read time
except day counts against `as_of`.

execution.title: Execution
execution.description: NOT_REPORTED or USER_REPORTED. Never system verification.

OpportunityLifecycleItemOut.title: OpportunityLifecycleItemOut
OpportunityLifecycleItemOut.description: One opportunity, on seven axes that never collapse into one another.

OpportunityLifecycleOut.title: OpportunityLifecycleOut
OpportunityLifecycleOut.description:
The whole contract.

`opportunity_authority` carries the OPPORTUNITY family's standing, so an
empty `opportunities` list is never read as "you have no opportunities"
when the truth is that no governing run exists.

resource_capacities.title: Resource Capacities
resource_capacities.description: Declared shared-pool capacities by resource code; omitted pools use governed defaults where product rules define one.

OptimizationRequest.title: OptimizationRequest
OptimizationRequest.description:
Start an optimization run over a completed analysis.

`resource_capacities` is the existing typed user-constraint contract the
orchestrator seals into the spec hash: shared-pool capacities the taxpayer
declares (e.g. FHSA_ROOM carry-forward). Nothing here can name an engine
input or supply a computation.

PortfolioExclusionOut.title: PortfolioExclusionOut
PortfolioExclusionOut.description: Why something is NOT recommended — itself a result, never hidden.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why nothing was generated, when nothing was.

ProjectionResponse.title: ProjectionResponse
ProjectionResponse.description:
Always an object with a STATUS, never a bare null.

A null would leave the caller unable to tell "no rule authorized a
projection" from "the feature is off" from "something went wrong". Each of
those is a different fact and each gets its own status.

ProjectionUncertaintyOut.title: ProjectionUncertaintyOut
ProjectionUncertaintyOut.description: A projection's uncertainty is stated, not implied by a single number.

RecordDecisionRequest.title: RecordDecisionRequest
RecordDecisionRequest.description:
Declare intent. PROCEED means the user decided to proceed — it is not,
and is never treated as, evidence that anything happened.

contribution_room.title: Contribution Room
contribution_room.description: Known available room, when the taxpayer has it to state.

RegisteredAccountIn.title: RegisteredAccountIn
RegisteredAccountIn.description:
An ACTUAL registered-account contribution record — a taxpayer fact.

Distinct from a scenario lever: this states money already contributed in
the tax year, and it enters the baseline analysis. A lever models a
contribution not yet made. Only the deduction-bearing account types the
engine computes today are accepted.

action_date.title: Action Date
action_date.description: The date the user says the action happened, if they choose to say. Validated for sanity; never rewrites the server's own recorded_at.

ReportActionRequest.title: ReportActionRequest
ReportActionRequest.description: The user reports having acted. Self-report, recorded verbatim.

current_snapshot_hash.title: Current Snapshot Hash
current_snapshot_hash.description: Echo this to acknowledge the state described here. It is the optimistic-concurrency token.

RetentionChangesOut.title: RetentionChangesOut
RetentionChangesOut.description:
The whole contract.

`baseline_status` is NO_BASELINE on first use, and `changes` is then empty
by design: with nothing acknowledged there is no prior authoritative state,
and describing the user's existing position as a list of arrivals would
report events that never happened.

ScenarioComparisonOut.title: ScenarioComparisonOut
ScenarioComparisonOut.description:
Deltas kept SEPARATE by concept.

Objective, tax, refund/balance, cash commitment and effect-type differences
each answer a different question. Folding them into one "difference" would
make a timing benefit and a permanent reduction look like the same thing.

ScenarioContextOut.title: ScenarioContextOut
ScenarioContextOut.description:
Scenario metadata appropriate for customer display.

Enough to title and date the comparison. No internal storage identifiers, no
document ids, no object keys.

label.title: Label
label.description: Descriptive only. Excluded from the scenario hashes, so renaming never changes identity or invalidates evidence.

ScenarioCreateRequest.title: ScenarioCreateRequest
ScenarioCreateRequest.description:
Everything a caller may say about a scenario.

There is deliberately no field here through which an engine input could be
named or a computation supplied.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Educational information only. This is not tax advice, not a filing, and is not submitted to the CRA.

ScenarioReferenceOut.title: ScenarioReferenceOut
ScenarioReferenceOut.description:
Pinned identity of what informed the decision. References, not copies —
the sealed scenario remains the authority for its own content.

optimality_claim.title: Optimality Claim
optimality_claim.description: Always 'none'. This is a feasible, deterministic, engine-evaluated portfolio, not a globally optimal one.

optimality_note.title: Optimality Note
optimality_note.default: This is a feasible, deterministic, engine-evaluated strategy set. It is not a globally optimal portfolio.

display_support_score.title: Display Support Score
display_support_score.description: User-facing support score, 0-100. Not a probability.

assumption_adjusted_score.title: Assumption Adjusted Score
assumption_adjusted_score.description: Uncapped support after assumption uncertainty; ordering key.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: This is a support score: it reflects how well this result is backed by the information supplied, its documentation, and the published rule it relies on. It is not a probability that the CRA will accept a claim, and not a probability of receiving the amount shown.

SupportScore.title: SupportScore
SupportScore.description:
A support/reliability score — NOT a probability.

Named `support` throughout the API for that reason. The disclaimer travels
with the value so no surface can present it as a likelihood of CRA
acceptance or of receiving the amount shown.

TaxAssuranceOut.title: TaxAssuranceOut
TaxAssuranceOut.description:
The whole contract.

`attention` orders opportunity `source_id`s in documented review-next
order: urgency band, then closable-gap band, then the optimizer's own
sealed rank, then identity. It is a presentation order, not an optimum.

UploadRequest.title: UploadRequest
UploadRequest.description:
Bounded at the schema, so an oversized field is refused by the parser
before a handler ever builds a string out of it.
